h1: 3-in-1 shear, brake and roll machines — 8″ to 80″
intro: A 3-in-1 machine puts a shear, a brake and a slip roll on one frame: the starter machine for the small sheet-metal, HVAC and hobby shop, and the compact machine for a maintenance department that cuts, folds and rolls a few parts a day. NovoTech sells two kinds in Canada, both on this page: hand-operated 3-in-1 machines from 8″ to 52″, 20 to 16 ga, with a guillotine shear, a finger brake and three rolls on one bench frame; and the motorized E3-IN-1 that shears 1/8″, bends 14 ga and rolls 12 ga over 52 and 80″ with a 4.7 HP motor. Every model is in the table below with its width, capacity and weight, then each family with its full specification and photos. NovoTech's value-line machines are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Is a 3-in-1 machine as good as three separate machines?
faq.a: No — it is as good as the three machines a small shop would otherwise not have. The shear, brake and roll share one frame and one capacity rating, so each is lighter than a dedicated machine of the same width, and changing from one function to another takes a minute. For a shop that cuts, folds and rolls a few parts a day in 20 – 16 ga it is the right buy; for production, buy the dedicated shear, box and pan brake and slip roll.

By the widest sheet you cut or fold in one piece: the 12″ and 24″ models for enclosures and small parts, 40″ and 52″ for duct and panel work, 80″ (E3-IN-1) for full sheets. The capacity — 20 to 16 ga on the hand-operated models, 1/8″ shear and 14 ga brake on the motorized — is the same across the width.

faq.q: How small a cylinder can it roll?
faq.a: The minimum rolling diameter is set by the roll diameter and is listed per model in the table; the slip roll section also has grooves for wire and the top roll lifts to slip the finished cylinder off.

faq.q: How are the capacities rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?
faq.a: In gauge of mild steel over the full width; stainless about two gauges lighter, aluminum about two gauges heavier. The hand-operated models rate copper, brass and aluminum separately in the specification table.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
